newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed as specs roll spots forward.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed as specs roll spots forward.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed Tuesday as speculators rolled the spot December contract forward ahead of its first notice day, market sources said.
"If you did not roll you were sidelined for the day," one trader said. "We all anticipated this would happen sooner or later."
December contract, which goes into a month-long notice period Nov 19, ended down 1.75 cents at 118.20 cents a lb after ranging from 120.70 to 116.80.
Most-active March ended 1.30 higher at 110.40 after trading from 110.50 to 108.40. The back months closed up 1.45 to 1.55.
The widely watched December/March switch shrunk to 7.80 cents, down from 10.85 cents at the close on Monday.
On the charts, near-term support in the December contract was seen at 116.80, a low seen last week, with the next level noted at 114.00. March support was pegged at 107.50.
Although traders said tight nearby supplies would continue to underpin values, they said the latest drawdown in exchange-certfied stocks had little effect on the market.
"Half of nothing is nothing," a trader said.

CSCE reported after the close of business Monday U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 471 60-kg bags in the week ended Nov 8 to 333 bags -- or less than two lots of coffee, the lowest level since the exchange started tracking inventories in 1980.
Traders also downplayed data showing 1,200 60-kg bags of coffee were pending grading, saying it not enough coffee to impact the short supply situation.
Open interest on the December contract was down 563 lots as of Monday at 8,483 lots -- the equivalent of more than two million bags of coffee.

Meanwhile, the head of Colombia's National Exporters' Association, Gabriel Rosas Vega, said Tuesday he expected the country's output to come in at no more than 10.5 to 11 million 60-kg bags of coffee during the current coffee year, down from 12.9 million bags in the 1995-1996 coffee year.
Rosas said production would be adversely affected in part by the imminent closure of the heavily indebted National Coffee Fund, which has been hard hit by the recent strength of Colombia's peso.
The day's volume reached an estimated 10,731 lots.
